summary: The R&D workstation resolved files-sync-share.net, a rare storage-themed domain, before the seed alert.
The workstation opened a short TLS session to the rare storage edge before the larger transfer sequence.
Seed JA4 alert matched a suspicious TLS beacon to the rare storage edge.
PowerShell launched from the user profile and invoked a staging script under C:\Users\analyst\AppData\Roaming\sync.ps1.
Archive utility 7z.exe created RND-Q2-prototype.zip from a project workspace shortly before outbound transfer.
The newly created RND-Q2-prototype.zip was staged under C:\Users\Public\Music\cache.dat for transfer.
A large outbound HTTPS upload to files-sync-share.net followed the archive creation, with roughly 640 MB sent.
DLP recorded the encrypted outbound transfer size but could not inspect the archive contents.
The same workstation resolved api.files-sync-share.net, a sibling domain on the same storage edge.
A follow-on TLS session used the sibling API domain after the large upload completed.
A second R&D workstation briefly connected to the same storage edge, but only once and without host corroboration.
ws-rnd-09 had an approved backup job running in the same hour, explaining some storage-oriented traffic.
Normal corporate SharePoint sync traffic from ws-rnd-04 was also present during the investigation window.
EDR did not preserve the full PowerShell command line, limiting reconstruction of the staging script.
A lab workstation reached the same IP through a different vendor CDN domain, indicating the IP is not uniquely malicious.
